ledger.note: 555: the Yenisei Kyrgyz (Cliopatria's start). The page dates no founding: the Kyrgyz 're-emerged associated with other Turkic peoples in the 6th century' and 'by the fall of the Göktürk Empire in the 8th century ... had established their own thriving state'; Han sources name them Gekun (2nd c. BCE) and Jiankun, and the Xiongnu conquered them 'around 202 BCE'. They are Göktürk subjects from Muqan's reign (553-572).

wars.name: Türk campaign against the Kyrgyz
wars.outcome: Second Turkic Khaganate page: Türk forces 'inflicted a crushing defeat on the Yenisei Kyrgyz'; the Kyrgyz ruler Bars Beg 'fell in battle' and his descendants 'were to remain vassals of the Göktürks for several generations'. No land is named.
wars.note: The Turkic suzerainty belongs in the Second Turkic Khaganate's dossier (vassal_start 710, counterpart yenisei-kyrgyz); that state has no row.

wars.name: Uyghur conquest of the Kyrgyz
wars.outcome: Bayanchur 'destroyed several of their trading outposts before defeating a Kyrgyz army and executing their khan' (Uyghur page); 'the Kyrgyz came under the rule of the Uyghur Khaganate' (Yenisei Kyrgyz page). The Uyghur page also lists the Kyrgyz among peoples 'brought ... under Uyghur rule' (747, citation needed).
wars.note: The Uyghur dossier (ia-01, uyghur-khaganate) should carry the vassal tint 758-840.

wars.name: Kyrgyz conquest of the Uyghur Khaganate
wars.outcome: Qasar seized the Uyghur throne in 839 with Shatuo help; his rival Kulug Bagha called in the Kyrgyz, who sacked Ordu-Baliq in 840 and beheaded Qasar. 'The Yenisei Kyrgyz and Tang dynasty launched a successful war between 840 and 848 against the Uyghur Khaganate.'
wars.note: Yenisei Kyrgyz page: 'On February 13, 843 at Kill the Foreigners Mountain, the Tang Chinese inflicted a devastating defeat on the Uyghur qaghan's forces'; in 845 and 847 Tang emperors gave titles to Kyrgyz khagans (Kyrgyz Khaganate page).

certainty.note: Forest and mountain frontiers throughout; the pages date no treaty line. The Baikal and Orkhon reaches after 840 are contested between the Uyghur page and Drompp (Kyrgyz Khaganate page).

notes: Cliopatria row Yenisei Kyrgyz 555..1219 (9 shapes, a gap 763-792). Not split: the pages show one people with phases (Turkic subjects to 840, the khaganate 840-925 with its own article, an autonomous country to the Mongol submission of 1207/1208) rather than successive states, and the khaganate article's infobox (840-925, 'Succeeded by: Liao dynasty') is contradicted by Drompp (diplomatic relations only in 924, no conflict) and by the 1207/1208 submission. Cliopatria draws one fixed polygon for 555-762 and 850-1205; the homeland statement of the page is matched by only 25% of Tuva and 2% of Khakassia, so every shape is corrected (Irkutsk removed before 840, Tuva and Khakassia added). Status as vassal is not recorded in this dossier (the suzerain's ledger carries vassal_start with the Kyrgyz as counterpart): needed in gokturk-khaganate (written, 553-586), eastern-gokturks (587-630: the pages are silent on the Kyrgyz in these years), second-turkic-khaganate (from 710, no dossier), uyghur-khaganate (758-840, ia-01 part d) and mongol-empire (from 1208). The Kyrgyz page gives no area (infobox silent), so no ratio. The dossier ends at 1208, not 1219; the Cliopatria 1210 and 1216 shapes are marked wrong for that reason and the Mongol dossier should take over the land. Pages disagree on the Orkhon after 840 (Khitans 890 versus no presence after the 840s). Counterparts needing dossiers: second-turkic-khaganate (682-744). Page budget: five pages, all cited.
